competences: The learner identifies key facts about roles of the central government.
The learner explains information about Types of government and roles of the central government using reference texts.
languageCompetence: Pronounces, spells, reads and writes central government, government, administration.
objectives: By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to identify facts about roles of the central government.
By the end of the lesson, learners should be able to answer the available sourced questions about Types of government and roles of the central government.
priorKnowledge: Learners have already studied Uganda and related Social Studies concepts. They build on this earlier work to learn about roles of the central government.
materials: Chart showing roles of the central government
Primary Five SST reference on Types of government and roles of the central government
references: P.5 Social Studies Lesson Notes Term III: Uganda as an Independent Nation

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher recalls the previous SST topic and introduces roles of the central government. They ask "Mention the types of government in Uganda." and listen to learners' first responses before referring to the source notes.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners recall previously studied content and answer the opening question, explaining their ideas in short sentences.

steps.stage: Development: Meaning and key facts about roles of the central government
steps.content: This is the government that bears all the major responsibilities towards the people in a country. Differences between the central government and local government Central government Local government Central government is one ▪ Local governments are many. The National (central) government. It is one government. There are many local governments. Central government is one government while local government has many local government Central government runs major hospitals while local government controls dispensaries and health centres. Central government builds major roads while local government maintains feeder roads Party system of government.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about roles of the central government on the chalkboard, including "This is the government that bears all the major responsibilities towards the people in a country. Differences between the central government and local government Central government". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Features and related facts about roles of the central government
steps.content: Democratic system of government. Unitary government system. Monarchial government system Theocratic system of government. Dictatorship system of government Federal system of government Military system of government. Decentralization is the transfer of some powers from the central government to the local government. The central government is ruled by the president while the local governments are led by chair persons for local council 5.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about roles of the central government on the chalkboard, including "Democratic system of government.; Unitary government system.". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.stage: Development: Further facts about roles of the central government
steps.content: Establishment of many government and private universities e.g. Mbarara university, Bugema university, Mbale university , KIU etc Corruption in some government departments. Inspector general of government (IGG) In which one way did Amin’s government violate human rights Local council I Village Cell LC I They are all under the National government. It controls all armed forces. It cares for the development of the whole nation. Runs the major hospitals. Builds and maintains major roads.
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher writes the documented points about roles of the central government on the chalkboard, including "Establishment of many government and private universities e.g. Mbarara university, Bugema university, Mbale university , KIU etc; Corruption in some government departments.". They explain the relevant facts and check learners' understanding with direct questions.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners read the source-backed statements, explain the key words, respond to questions and copy the points into their books.

steps.content: Mention the types of government in Uganda. | Why is the government of Uganda dividing the country into many districts? | Give two differences in the activities run by the central and local government. | What is the ruling body of government called? | Who is the local of all ministers in government?
steps.teacherActivity: The teacher gives the original questions, starting with "Mention the types of government in Uganda." and "Why is the government of Uganda dividing the country into many districts?". They monitor pupils as they answer, check responses against the source material and provide corrections.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners answer the sourced exercise questions independently, consult their copied notes and correct any mistakes after marking.

steps.teacherActivity: The teacher reviews the factual content on roles of the central government, asks "Mention the types of government in Uganda." and follows up with "Why is the government of Uganda dividing the country into many districts?". They confirm the answers and assign the remaining sourced practice.
steps.learnerActivity: Learners state one important fact from their lesson notes, answer the final oral questions and correct their written work.

assessment: Use the original questions "Mention the types of government in Uganda." and "Why is the government of Uganda dividing the country into many districts?", along with other listed items, to assess learners' understanding and correct errors from the source material.
homework: Answer the remaining sourced question, including "What role do civil servants play in government?"
